chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Al-Nuhayki, from Mansur ibn Yunus, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) saying:
Three things that do no harm: Al-Raziqi grapes, sugar cane, and Lebanese apples.

key_terms.لَا تَضُرُّ: do no harm (free from impurity or defect)

ai.seo_question: What are the three specific foods mentioned by Imam Musa al-Kadhim that are free from harm?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) identifies three specific foods—Al-Raziqi grapes, sugar cane, and Lebanese apples—as free from ritual or physical impurity (*la taḍurru*). This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the inherent purity of natural, high-quality produce, distinguishing them from items that may carry specific ritual concerns or physical defects.
